title: Avengers: Doomsday breaks Disney trailer record but Spider-Man remains ahead
body_md:
The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday generated 563 million views during its first 24 hours, according to the figures reported in the historical news feed. That performance establishes a new Disney trailer record and places the upcoming Marvel ensemble among the most closely watched movie marketing campaigns of the year.

However, the record comes with an important distinction. Spider-Man: Brand New Day reportedly attracted 718.6 million views during its own opening 24-hour period. That leaves Doomsday in second place overall, with a difference of 155.6 million views between the two trailers.

The comparison is notable because both productions feature characters associated with Marvel's cinematic universe, yet their commercial and distribution contexts are different. Spider-Man's achievement does not contradict the claim that Doomsday has established a record for Disney specifically.

Trailer viewership provides a useful measure of initial attention, but it is not a direct measurement of ticket sales or unique audience size. Repeat viewing, distribution across platforms, promotional timing and the size of existing fan communities can all influence the reported totals. A successful campaign must ultimately translate attention into attendance.

The latest Doomsday footage has renewed discussion about returning characters and their relationships within the franchise. Robert Downey Jr.'s appearance as Doctor Doom is an especially significant element of the film's marketing because audiences previously associated the actor with Tony Stark.

The involvement of characters connected to the X-Men also gives the production a broader appeal across different eras of Marvel screen adaptations. The challenge for the filmmakers is to make that extensive history meaningful without allowing familiarity alone to overwhelm the story.

Anthony and Joe Russo are directing the film, which is scheduled to open on December 18, 2026. The release represents a major test of Marvel's ability to bring viewers back for a large-scale Avengers event after years without a new entry under that title.

Whether the film can outperform Brand New Day commercially remains an open question. Reviews, audience recommendations, repeat attendance and competition during the theatrical window will matter alongside the initial enthusiasm generated by the trailer.

It would therefore be premature to interpret either the Disney record or the overall second-place ranking as a reliable forecast of the eventual box office outcome.

What the latest figures establish is that the studio has secured extraordinary visibility for its upcoming release. The next milestone will be whether that visibility produces sustained demand once audiences can actually watch the movie.

Which film do you expect to finish ahead at the box office: Doomsday or Brand New Day?
